countingRules.commits: Every commit reachable from main, the merge commit included.
countingRules.firstParentCommits: Commits on main's first-parent line: the merge counts once and the two commits of the feature branch do not appear.
countingRules.hotspotCommits: Non-merge commits reachable from main (the feature branch's commits included) whose own diff changes services/orders/internal/application/order_service.go. Merge commits are never counted. The file has no rename.
countingRules.coChange: Each non-merge commit reachable from main counts once for services/orders/internal/pricing/pricing.go and tax.go: pricingTogether changes both, pricingOnly changes pricing.go but not tax.go, taxOnly the reverse. Merge commits are not counted. Neither file is renamed.
countingRules.rename: services/orders/src/order.go -> services/orders/internal/domain/order.go is one identity (git reports R100); the move commit is counted once for the file, and its history before the move belongs to the same file.
countingRules.dependencies: direct and dev are the keys of dependencies and devDependencies in package.json; packages are the entries of package-lock.json "packages" except the root ""; devOnlyPackages have "dev": true.
countingRules.dateAnomaly: A commit whose committer date is earlier than a parent's committer date; exactly one exists.

items.expectedWikiStatement: Orders consumes payments.events in consumer group "orders" and turns payment.captured, payment.failed and payment.refunded into order events. Duplicates are handled only by comparing the current status with the status the event leads to: a repeat that arrives while the order is still in that status is ignored, but a repeated capture after shipment fails the transition. The consumer commits the offset even when applying the event failed (the failure is only logged), so a failed event is not redelivered.

judge.readerTask: Describe how orders reacts to payment events.
mustShow: offset committed even when applying fails
